reviews.text: This app used to be so simple. Take a picture and that’s it. Now there’s so many options for people like me who only need one. Love the thought of using an emoji next to the meal to see how one felt afterwards.

reviews.title: Best Simple Food Journal Around
reviews.text: I’ve been using this app since 2020, honestly, it’s been great. There’s not too much going on, probably best food journal there is if you value simplicity and consistency.

reviews.title: Love it
reviews.text: Been using AteMate for a long time. I really enjoy keeping track of my meals with the app. It’s very simple and user friendly.

reviews.title: The photo analysis function always has negative feedback
reviews.text:
Update on 9/10/26: I just tried this app again after many months and many updates and they have changed and fixed nothing. The AI feature never gets the food right and you can't tell it what's in the picture. The whole point of logging food and journaling food is so you can go back and see what you ate that day or see patterns in your food so the log not being right is an issue. Yes, I understand you can add a note but the rest of the log is wrong and you can't change anything other than your note. The suggestions on what to change in the future are questionable at best because, again the food they think you're eating is wrong and the app is not worth the $10 a month minimum just to use it!!! Gave it a second chance and it's still the same awful app. The image-to-log feature is what most people are paying for and it sucks so I shouldn't be paying for a feature I can't use! 

2/24/25: The app is fine until you use the photo analysis feature. It will always tell you it's not good. The first few times I didnt care beacsue my meals were not as good as it could have been but even if you do the suggestions it says and you replace everything with the “better option” it still says its processed even if you made it from scratch or its high in sodium even if you used all low sodium or it not enough veggies or its high in sugar when there's no sugar. It will always say it's a bad meal. I know it's just suggestions but if they want you to pay for this and use this for best results don't make it shame you for every meal you eat. I was told that my fruit bowl was “too high in processed sugar and I should try something lighter next time”!!! How much lighter can I get than a single apple with a few grapes? The only meals that got a ok result were ones where I literally had a single grape in the picture. That's not how healthy eating works; it's not just eating as light as possible. I was getting so stressed trying to make the meals so they would pass this stupid analysis and it's not possible or healthy.

reviews.title: Good, but too much
reviews.text:
I really like this app, but I don't use any of the features aside from the photo journal. I have no interest in an AI coach, personally.

I wish there was a lower subscription tier with restricted features, but I understand that it might not be feasible/profitable. Unfortunately, for $9.99 per month, I just can't justify it when everything else is getting more and more expensive.

Kudos to the devs for making a great app.

reviews.title: Amazing App!
reviews.text: I used this app while I was losing weight after my first child. It helped me lose 30lbs! When I was pregnant with my second I had gestational diabetes and this app synced seamlessly with my blood sugar reader and I also used it to keep track of my steps and of course I use the photos to remember what I ate that day. Love it so much!

reviews.title: Fun alternative to counting calories
reviews.text: I really enjoy seeing my food through pictures as a way to be more accountable about what I’m eating everyday. It motivates me to add more color and variety to my diet - which encourages me to eat healthier overall. Random bonus: it’s nice to know for sure how old my leftovers are or when I opened that container of cream cheese lol!

reviews.title: Request for the developers
reviews.text:
1. Can we PLEASE have the option to return to square photos? I know it’s a visual thing but I can’t be alone in this. If it is possible to create a toggle in the settings to the new way or square I would love this feature. 

2. Can we get a fasting timer instead of it starting from the picture of our last meal? Since we already have the option to turn fasting on and off. I’ve been going in and changing the time to when I finished eating so that I can get a more accurate picture and it becomes cumbersome after a while. 

I throughly enjoy this app after being a long term original user before it became a subscription and I got miffed and left. I’ve been back for a few years since and I get it, gotta keep the app going somehow and I find it very helpful for my mindful eating habits.

reviews.title: Excellent for intermittent fasting

reviews.title: Great for Intuitive Eating
reviews.text: As someone who has a poor relationship with calorie counting but want to easily track what i eat for my diet, this app has been amazing for my needs! I’ve been using it for over a year now and i love it! I have the app for quick access as a widget on my lock screen. Friends think i’m just taking pic of my food but it’s really me tracking it for my diet! so sneaky and easy and sustainable ^^ I love that it also tracks my movement and weigh-in’s all visible in one place. Thank you for building this app! It’s the first app i’ve used consistently for so long, and look forward to viewing instead of dreading opening a page full of metrics ^^ the other apps were too overwhelming with too many things to input it was hard to keep up. The photos here help me with general accountability because i often forget what i eat. Helps me be honest if i’d been eating more off-path food than i thought.

reviews.title: Love the new AI journal analysis. So helpful!
reviews.text:
I have been using this app for a while and it has been a game changer. Nothing else worked for me in staying consistent and building lasting healthy habits. And now the new AI analysis helps me uncover both positive and negative behaviors that I might miss on my own.
With the constant updates and their commitment to privacy, this app is well worth the few dollars a month that the subscription costs. 
By the way, I don’t understand why people are complaining about the subscription and calling the app a scam. Did they read the description before downloading? It clearly states that it’s a subscription app with a free trial. 
Did they even try the app? It’s easy to use and extremely helpful. Thank you developers!

reviews.title: Not free- can’t take accountability
reviews.text: App that scams people to download it by pretending it’s free. It’s not at all. Lying developer.—if you don’t want to be called a liar or scammer then don’t try deceiving people. It’s simple. Most of your other reviews say the same thing, so it’s clear of your intent to waste others time. A transparent person would not make the consumer go through the whole process of signing up before informing them that they must pay to do literally anything with the app. Clearly you know most people do not check the app description, that’s why you ONLY put a disclaimer there. It is malicious to waste people’s time this way and trick them into downloading an app. Getting defensive over the reviews calling you out makes it worse by the way. It means you have transparency issues and bad customer service. However, have a good day. Hopefully you can present your app in a less annoying way in the future, then I would be willing to check it out. I recommend to make it clear that your service is not free upon opening the app. It’s much more courteous than prompting users to sign up immediately. Also whoever responds to the reviews is very condescending to whoever calls them out, even when the consumer has a reason to.

reviews.title: LOVE THIS APP!
reviews.text:
I’ve been on a diet roller coaster for most of my life. After losing about 40 pounds and then gain some of that back (again) I decided to get off the roller coaster for good. I decided to try intuitive eating.

After going it on my own got several months, I started looking for an app that would allow me to log my food without judgment, I didn’t want to worry about calories, being reminded to weigh my self or track my weight loss. There were other apps that were similar, but the ones that had the features I wanted were extremely expensive. One was $8.99 a week! ($467 a year!)

This app is perfect! It not only allows me to track what I eat, but I can reflect on each meal and how it made me feel without judging myself. I can now act as an outside observer as I learn to eat well and treat my body with care.

Here are the features I love:

1. You can track by taking a picture. Snap a picture and the app identifies the food. It isn’t perfect, but you can edit the food to what you actually ate.

2. Reflections- you can not only make notes on each meal, but you can reflect on the process later. You can create your own reflection Q & A and edit those as you need them.

3. The app works with Apple Health to track exercise.

The price at $50/year is very affordable for what you get.

reviews.title: Best Food Journal I’ve Ever Used
reviews.text:
I’ve been using Ate for several years and hands down it’s the best app I’ve ever used to keep track of the food and drinks I eat.

I’ve been tracking my food for a few decades and I started on paper, moved to a computer , and when the iPhone hit the market I was excited about the possibilities. Unfortunately it took many years and dozens of ill fated attempts to find the right app.

Ate is the perfect app. It doesn’t force me to use cumbersome systems and gives me just enough customization to make it my own.

Additionally, whenever I’ve had a question or made a recommendation, the people at Ate respond quickly and are responsive to my needs.

I love Ate!!

reviews.title: Nutritionist approved
reviews.text:
As a nutritionist, I know the macros to my food. I find it tedious and really unnecessary to log every single macro down to the milligram. Rather I focus on eating clean foods, and just logging what I ate, when I ate it, and how I felt 30 minutes after. This applies to fluids, exercise, sleep, and every other aspect of like. I enjoy the way ATE allows you to see your day in full. Rather then having to click on each log to read the notes. I also appreciate the ability to share your “day” with others. This helps for accountability, but also for doctors. In a day where technology is booming, having that ability is extremely helpful. 

I will recommend this app to my clients.

reviews.title: Everything I wanted more
reviews.text:
This is one of the best apps I’ve ever downloaded. I was looking for an app to help practice my intuitive eating and this had everything I wanted done even better than I imagined it could be done. Every time they add a new feature, it’s always something that I didn’t even know that I really wanted.

I’m hesitant signing up for sub subscriptions, but this one has been worth it and I keep coming back to it because it’s just built so well!

reviews.title: This is the one!
reviews.text: This is the app I’ve been looking for. The camera implementation is great, and the AI does its best to decipher what you’ve got on your plate. It’s not always on the money, but it gives you a good start on ingredient analysis. This app is flexible, non-judgmental, and open-ended so you can experiment with different nutrition strategies and approaches to eating. You can even make up your own! I LOVE THIS APP!! I love the “eat the rainbow” approach to nutrition. Great app, highly recommended.

reviews.title: loving it so far

reviews.title: Awesome
reviews.text:
It doesn’t harass you, it doesn’t berate you, but with a great interface it stubs you gently into the direction you want to go. 

Very easy to track and instead of calorie counting you can see the quality of your foss choices in rainbow colors (you can track standard sugar, fast, carbs if you prefer). You can enter via text or take a photo and AI does the rest. You can add notes and track feelings and so on.

This app is a very refreshing and a great surprise!

reviews.title: Only 1 complaint.
reviews.text:
The only complaint I have is that I can’t edit the AI analysis if the food. On my smoothie it said I ate “dairy” when that is completely false. I would also like to see a chart that shows me how much if each food category I’ve eaten in a day, a week, a month, a year, etc.

That being said, it’s a small detail. I’ve found the app useful overall.

reviews.title: A food journal that works for me!
reviews.text:
I’m just starting my intuitive eating journey but I can already notice some changes. First I’m actively noticing if I start wandering looking for a snack out of boredom-less nibbling already! Next I love the short and quick questions to thinking about what and why I was eating. I also love that drinking water and my daily movement also are logged on my path. 

Lastly, even if I have something that isn’t the greatest for me I love that it brings me back to the path. The meal I ate was “off path” not my life or my goals. The app doesn’t guilt you but instead encourages you to reflect.

My only suggestion right now would be the option to log food groups. I’d like the ability to see how well rounded each of my meals was. 😊

reviews.title: Almost perfect
reviews.text:
I have revised my review a few times this week and the rating has increased because as the days go by, I either figure out or find features I need. I really like that it tracks fasting for intermittent fasting. I like that it doesn’t focus on calories or macros, plenty of aps for that and in real life, one has to
learn what is good and not. I like this helps track for accountability and to see how Im doing. I like the helpful articles, I like how it allows tracking of things like emotions, locations, what is happening around me and tendencies. I like that Im able to add a note based on what is meaningful to me at the moment. I can note nutritional info or how Im feeling or an explanation or all. I like the recaps, I like the “on path” “off path” as it allows for reflection of what Im eating.

reviews.title: Unique and wonderful!
reviews.text: I don’t want to count calories. I want something sustainable, and something tailored to me and my personal reactions to food. And I want something that encourages real mindfulness. This app has it all. It is the only thing like it on the market. Please never stop being the only real alternative to calorie counters on the market!!

reviews.text: I appreciate the simplicity of this app but didn’t realize the insights were limited to 10 days when I purchased. I have trouble with consistency and would like to be able to look at what I do enter over periods of longer than 10 days, to try and find trends.
